evidence.claim: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.title: Anayasa | Anayasa Mahkemesi
evidence.excerpt: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text governing the 2022 presidency; direct and stable legal authority/constraint source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Erdoğan's office-level authority and checks in 2022; not a claim about personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same articles constrain decree power and preserve parliamentary/judicial checks.
Formal authority does not prove how he used it in practice.

evidence.claim: NATO says the United States maintains absolute control and custody of forward-deployed nuclear weapons in Europe, while Allies retain political control of nuclear deterrence and NATO remains committed to arms control, disarmament, and non-proliferation.
evidence.title: NATO’s nuclear deterrence policy and forces
evidence.excerpt: NATO says the United States maintains absolute control and custody of forward-deployed nuclear weapons in Europe, while Allies retain political control of nuclear deterrence and NATO remains committed to arms control, disarmament, and non-proliferation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Current NATO topic page directly states custody, control, and the alliance's nuclear policy framework.
evidence.period_fit: Stable alliance structure relevant to 2022 and beyond.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows Erdoğan did not control nuclear weapons independently; any role was alliance-level and indirect.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove Turkey lacked all influence inside NATO consultations.
The page is current, so the wording is not a 2022 snapshot.

evidence.claim: The NPG is NATO's senior nuclear consultation body, covering policy, doctrine, planning, force posture, capabilities, exercises, and safety/security; all Allies except France are members, and decisions are by consensus.
evidence.title: Nuclear Planning Group (NPG)
evidence.excerpt: The NPG is NATO's senior nuclear consultation body, covering policy, doctrine, planning, force posture, capabilities, exercises, and safety/security; all Allies except France are members, and decisions are by consensus.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO governance page describing nuclear decision structure and consultation rules.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Turkey, as a NATO Ally, participated in consultation rather than unilateral nuclear command.
contrary_evidence: Membership does not equal unilateral control.

evidence.claim: Türkiye signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty on 24 September 1996 and ratified it on 16 February 2000; the treaty is still not in force.
evidence.title: Status of Signatures and Ratifications
evidence.excerpt: Türkiye signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty on 24 September 1996 and ratified it on 16 February 2000; the treaty is still not in force.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Treaty-status table from the CTBTO is the authoritative status source.
evidence.period_fit: Valid status for 2022 and current comparison.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows a formal non-testing, nonproliferation commitment inherited and maintained in Erdoğan's era, not a personal achievement by itself.
contrary_evidence: CTBT ratification does not itself prove day-to-day restraint or crisis prudence.
The treaty is not yet in force, so legal effect is limited.

evidence.claim: Türkiye has an NPT safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol in force with the IAEA, which strengthens verification over declared nuclear material and activities.
evidence.title: Country List: Türkiye, Republic of
evidence.excerpt: Türkiye has an NPT safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol in force with the IAEA, which strengthens verification over declared nuclear material and activities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA country fact sheet listing treaty and safeguards status.
evidence.period_fit: Valid for 2022 and current status context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports the view that Turkey's nuclear posture is embedded in international verification, not unilateral national weapon control.
contrary_evidence: Safeguards are about peaceful-use verification, not a blanket guarantee of prudent state behavior.
The page does not say anything about Erdoğan personally.

evidence.claim: Incirlik Air Base in Turkey was described as the largest nuclear weapons storage site in Europe, located close to war-torn Syria, with security upgrades underway because of longstanding security concerns.
evidence.title: Upgrades At US Nuclear Bases In Europe Acknowledge Security Risk
evidence.excerpt: Incirlik Air Base in Turkey was described as the largest nuclear weapons storage site in Europe, located close to war-torn Syria, with security upgrades underway because of longstanding security concerns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical open-source analysis from a specialist organization, but adversarial and partly inferential.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Helps separate the inherited NATO storage posture from Erdoğan's personal choices.
contrary_evidence: The piece is older than 2022 and partly normative.
It describes US/NATO storage arrangements more than Turkish decision-making.

evidence.claim: The 2022 Strategic Concept says NATO faces a deteriorated security environment, identifies Russia as the most significant threat, and names the erosion of arms control, disarmament, and non-proliferation architectures as a challenge.
evidence.title: Strategic Concepts
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Strategic Concept says NATO faces a deteriorated security environment, identifies Russia as the most significant threat, and names the erosion of arms control, disarmament, and non-proliferation architectures as a challenge.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO strategic text and explanatory page for the 2022 security environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Background context for Erdoğan's alliance environment rather than a Turkey-specific nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: It is alliance context, not a ruler-specific conduct record.
It does not show Erdoğan personally advancing disarmament.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
